target_customer: Financial advisors, asset managers and brokerages that buy options-based defined outcome products and technology
problem: Retail and advisor clients wanted a defined return profile with limited downside, but derivative strategies were complex and hard to access.
business_model: Asset management fees on mutual funds, ETFs, UITs and managed accounts, plus technology services for brokerages
product_category: Target outcome (defined outcome) investment products and options-based asset management

founders.name: Karan Sood
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as a financial engineer. Cboe release says he remained CEO after the 2016 investment.

founders.name: Jeff Chang
education: McDonough School of Business, Georgetown University
founders.background_notes: CFA charterholder, per the YC page. Cboe release says he co-founded Vest in 2012 with Karan Sood.

exit.acquirer: CBOE Holdings (majority equity investment, making Vest a majority-owned subsidiary)
exit.reason: Price and stake size undisclosed. The release says earlier investors Y Combinator, Payment Ventures and First Round Capital had exited.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building options overlays with defined caps and buffers, and getting them into regulated fund wrappers, took financial engineering and compliance skill more than software research.

defensibility.rationale: Registered adviser status, fund structures and track record created some barrier, but the strategy concept was copied. Innovator launched buffer ETFs in 2018 and others followed, per a search summary of buffer ETF history.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cboe took a majority stake in January 2016. Competitors including Innovator later launched buffer ETFs in 2018.

market_need_then: Cboe Vest says the idea grew from the decline of the structured notes market after the 2008 financial crisis, leaving demand for defined outcome exposure outside bank notes.

branding.domain_note: Company site is vestfin.com, not vest.com.

identity.logo: Not described in the sources found
identity.voice_and_tone: Engineering Investment Outcomes; Wall Street rigor with Silicon Valley ingenuity (company site)

branding.brand_signature: Target Outcome Investments, a registered trademark phrase

rebrands.to: Cboe Vest (co-branded after Cboe majority stake; reverted to Vest on the current company site)
rebrands.why: Cboe ownership; the sequence is only inferred from search snippets

brand_strength.rationale: A short real word name is easy to remember but confusable with several other firms named Vest, and there was no evidence of consumer brand pull. The brand worked mainly through institutional credibility.

outcome_analysis: Vest created defined outcome products in 2013 and joined YC in Winter 2015. Cboe took a majority stake in January 2016 after earlier investors exited, and the company later pointed to partnerships with Cboe and First Trust and grew to tens of billions under management as buffer ETFs became a popular category. The company sells derivatives based strategies through regulated wrappers, which suits experienced finance founders, and the category tailwind after 2018 helped.
notes: Competition list left empty: no source dated near the 2015 batch naming competitors was found. A Seedtable entry for an August 2015 seed round with Y Combinator, First Round Capital and Payment Ventures was seen only in a search snippet and is unverified; amount unknown. The Cboe investment is a majority equity investment, so the YC status Acquired is treated as an acquisition. Assets under management figures on the YC page and company site (about $64B to $76B in 2026) are dated 2026 and are not founding facts. Later ownership changes were not found; the YC page mentions private equity backing, which was not verified. The rebrand entry is from search snippets and not dated.
